title: Optimize Automation: idempotent apply endpoints and webhook choreography
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: Customers using Redwood Optimize need a safe, observable, and retry-tolerant way to apply batching/caching configuration recommendations to serving fleets. Current manual flows are error-prone and risk partial application or double-apply scenarios when retries occur (eg. network blips, webhook redelivery).

Goal: Design and implement API and SDK primitives for: (1) an idempotent 'apply recommendation' endpoint with strong exactly-once semantics (best-effort within region/tenant), (2) a webhook delivery and acknowledgement protocol that supports retries and dead-lettering, and (3) client SDK helpers that make safe apply/rollback patterns easy for Optimize automation consumers. The implementation must preserve ability to rollback changes on failure, provide traceable audit events, and be compatible with Dedicated/Private modes.

Scope: API endpoints, webhook contract, idempotency strategy (tokens + dedupe store), SDK helpers (Go/TS), integration tests, migration guidance for existing automation, observability hooks and runbook updates. Not in scope: changes to core serving kernel selection logic or model-level quantization recommendations themselves (these are upstream of this work).
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent POST /v1/optimize/apply that accepts apply bundles and an idempotency_token; repeated requests with same token must not create duplicate apply operations and must return the same operation resource or terminal error.

Webhook contract: Optimize control plane sends events (apply.requested, apply.status, rollback.requested) with delivery semantics documented; receiver can respond with 2xx to ack or 4xx/5xx to trigger retry according to exponential backoff guidelines.

SDK helpers (TS + Go) provide 'ApplyWithRetries' and 'SafeRollback' primitives encapsulating token generation, exponential backoff, and idempotency token reuse; examples published in the public SDK repo.

Backend persists auditable operation record per apply with inputs, outputs, actor, and deterministic operation id; UI/console surfaces operation timeline and allow manual rollback when in terminal failed state.
Automated integration tests simulate duplicate delivery, partial failure mid-apply, and locked resource scenarios; system recovers to consistent state and emits monitoring signals for SLO breaches.
Migration guide that instructs existing customers on switching to the new endpoint with minimal disruption is published in docs and linked in console recommendations.
Security review completed and KMS signing for webhook payloads validated for Private deployments.
implementation_notes: API: POST /v1/optimize/apply - body: {apply_bundle, idempotency_token, requested_by, dry_run=false, rollback_on_error=true}. Returns 202 with operation_id or 200 with idempotent result if already completed.
Operation resource: GET /v1/optimize/operations/{id} returns status (PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ROLLED_BACK), events[], started_at, finished_at, outcome_blob (link to S3/secure store).

Idempotency: Use a per-tenant idempotency key namespace hashed to a dedupe table (TTL 7 days). On conflict, return stored operation reference. Use conditional write semantics in Postgres (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) backed by Redis lease for short-lived locks during apply execution to avoid concurrent executors proceeding in parallel.

Exactly-once semantics: Best-effort within a region/tenant. We do NOT attempt global consensus across regions for now; cross-region retries should use same token and will route to primary region where token was first accepted.

Webhook contract: POST body includes event_type, operation_id, sequence_number, payload, signature. Receiver must respond with 200 OK to acknowledge. Retries: exponential backoff up to 7 days with jitter; after N attempts (configurable default 10) event goes to DLQ and we emit alert.
Webhook signing: HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant secret stored in KMS (Private: customer-managed KMS), include timestamp and signature header to mitigate replay attacks.

Rollback: When rollback_on_error=true, the orchestrator will attempt automatic rollback steps using stored compensating actions. If rollback fails, mark operation as ROLLBACK_FAILED and surface manual rollback playbook in console.
SDK: Provide utility to generate idempotency tokens (UUIDv4 + tenant prefix + timestamp truncated) and to persist token-to-operation mapping locally for 24h to support client retries after restarts.
Retries: Client-side should never retry blindly without token reuse. Recommend deterministic token strategy for idempotency across restarts (e.g., persist token in task metadata).

Observability: Emit operation.lifecycle events to tracing (trace_id in operation), counter metrics (apply_requests_total, apply_duplicates, apply_failures, rollback_attempts), and histogram for apply_duration_ms. Add alerting thresholds for increases in apply_failures or DLQ backpressure.
Testing: Add chaos tests that drop webhook deliveries and simulate duplicate webhooks; run integration in Dedicated and Private QA clusters.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store: insert, conflict, read-after-write behaviour.
E2E test: submit apply with idempotency token, confirm single operation created; resubmit same token concurrently from two clients and assert single operation resource returned.
Webhook retry test: receiver returns 500 for first N-1 deliveries then 200; ensure event sequence is delivered and operation transitions correctly.
Rollback path test: fail mid-apply (simulate one component rejecting update) and verify automatic rollback runs and leaves system in pre-apply state.
Security test: signature validation failures result in 401 and do not process payload; replay window enforced.
Performance test: 95th percentile apply latency under typical recommendation sizes (bundles with 100 small rules) remains within runtime-1.20 SLO; measure token store throughput.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement endpoint behind feature flag; enable for internal teams and two pilot customers in Hosted region-us-west-2. Monitor metrics for duplicates and failures.
Phase 2 (broad): Enable for all hosted customers with throttled concurrency; release SDK helpers and migration guide.
Phase 3 (Dedicated/Private): Provide helm charts/ops playbook and KMS signing instructions; coordinate with customer success for enterprise rollouts.
Fallback: If new endpoint causes unexpected duplicate applies, feature flag off and run compensating rollback using recorded operation history.
